newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Election watchdog, Pollwatch, will seek 60 million baht from the government to set up a nationwide network and forums for the public to send their opinions to the Constitution Drafting Assembly (CDAO), Pollwatch chairman Gen Saiyudh Kerdphol said. However, Prime Minister Chavalit Yonchaiyudh immediately dismissed the request, saying the government already has its own working committee to handle public awareness capaigns on the charter and political reform. (THE NATION)

- Two men robbed a bank in Muang district here and shot a pursuing policemen to death on Tuesday. One of the robbers walked into the Bank of Ayudhaya's branch in Muang district here about 2.30 p.m. while his accomplice waited outside on a motorcycle with its engine running. The man approached a teller pretending he wanted to withdraw money but then whipped out a pistol and ordered all in the bank to kneel down. (BANGKOK POST)
- The Thai stock market yesterday dipped to its lowest level since September 1992, but a late rally overcome an almost 20-point deficit to push the set index back into positive territory at 819.79.

Still suffering the hangover of the deterioating asset quality of the banks and finance companies, the sagging property market and marcroeconomic stress, the stock market was depressed by a selling spree, which at one point brought the index down 19.30 points to 797.49. (THE NATION BUSINESS)

- Thailand's telecoms industry is predicted to grow rapidily in 1997, while more technology will be introdcued here, especially after a reduction of imported taxes on telecom equipment. Currently, the US government is trying to cut down tariffs on telecommunicaton products. If the deal is successful, telecom services will be expanded to middle and low-income consumers, said Dr Kosol Petchsuwan, secretary-general of the Telecommunications Association of Thailand. (BANGKOK POST)
